explain.say: Every year before Lunar New Year, Mei's grandmother in China shows her how to fold dumplings. Her grandmother learned from her own grandmother! Look at the board. It is a circle, because traditions go round and round through families.

explain.say: See the first stop, elders show? A tradition is a way of doing something that a group repeats over many years. It starts with older people showing younger ones, like folding dumplings or lighting diyas at Diwali. Who in your family shows you how to do things?

explain.say: Now look at children join and practise yearly. Children help and copy, and because the tradition happens every year, it sticks in their memory. Doing it together makes it feel special. What do you do every year in your family?

explain.say: See grow up and teach again? The children grow up and teach their own children, and the circle starts again. Each family may add a little twist, so traditions slowly change. Can you guess how many years a tradition can last this way?

explain.say: Some traditions are over a thousand years old, passed hand to hand like a relay baton. Traditions give people a sense of who they are and where they come from. Well done! Challenge: ask an elder about a tradition and find out who taught it to them.

faq.a: A tradition is a custom, belief or way of doing something that a group repeats and passes down over many years, like a festival meal, a song or a wedding custom.

faq.q: How do elders pass on traditions?
faq.a: Mostly by showing and doing, not just telling: cooking together, singing, telling stories, and inviting children to take part.

faq.q: Why do traditions happen every year?
faq.a: Repeating them at the same time each year, such as at a festival or harvest, helps everyone remember and gives the year a rhythm people look forward to.
Yes. Each generation may change small things, add new ideas or mix traditions from different cultures. That is how traditions stay alive.
Traditions connect people to their family and history, bring people together and give a sense of belonging and identity. Some people also choose to change or drop traditions they feel are unfair.
asks: What is the point of traditions?

facts: Lunar New Year is celebrated by well over a billion people across East and Southeast Asia and around the world.
The Olympic Games revived in 1896 a tradition from ancient Greece, where games were held from 776 BCE.

quiz.say: Why is the tradition picture drawn as a circle?

options.show: Children who learn it later teach their own children
options.say: Children who learn it later teach their own children

quiz.why: Each generation learns the tradition and then passes it on, so it keeps going round.

wrong.1: The circle shows the repeating path, not a shape of the tradition.
wrong.2: A tradition repeats many times; that is the whole idea.

quiz.say: What helps a tradition stick in memory?

options.show: It is written on a wall
options.say: It is written on a wall

quiz.why: Repeating it regularly, often at the same festival or season, makes it memorable.

wrong.0: Most traditions are shared, not hidden.
wrong.2: Traditions mostly live through doing them, not wall writing.
